subject: Combined Science
source: AQA GCSE Combined Science: Trilogy 8464 specification (2016 onwards) — Y11 covered topics across Biology B5–B7, Chemistry C6–C10, Physics P7–P8 with HT-only items flagged. Y10 content lives in aqa-combined-science-y10.json.

specPoints.specTitle: Homeostasis: maintenance of internal conditions; control of body temperature, water balance and blood glucose
Human nervous system: structure and function of CNS; receptors, sensory neurones, relay neurones, motor neurones; synapses
The endocrine system: glands and hormones; the pituitary as the 'master gland'; comparison of nervous and hormonal control
Control of blood glucose: insulin, glucagon (HT only) and Type 1 vs Type 2 diabetes
Hormones in human reproduction: menstrual cycle, contraception (hormonal and barrier), use of hormones to treat infertility (HT only — IVF detail)
Sexual and asexual reproduction; meiosis vs mitosis; advantages of each in different contexts
DNA structure as a polymer; the genome; genes coding for proteins; genetic code (HT only — protein synthesis from mRNA)
Inheritance: dominant and recessive alleles; genotype, phenotype, homozygous, heterozygous; Punnett square crosses
Inherited disorders: cystic fibrosis (recessive), polydactyly (dominant); ethical considerations of embryo screening
Variation and evolution: causes of variation; evolution by natural selection; speciation (HT only — full mechanism)
Selective breeding and genetic engineering; ethical and economic implications
Ecosystems: biotic and abiotic factors; competition; interdependence; food chains and trophic levels
Predator-prey cycles and population control
Biodiversity: importance and threats from pollution, deforestation, peat destruction, global warming
Carbon and water cycles; decomposers and decay (required practical investigating effect of temperature on rate of decay)
Rates of reaction: factors affecting rate (concentration, temperature, surface area, catalysts); calculation of mean rate from a graph
Collision theory: explanation of how factors above affect rate; Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution at different temperatures (HT only)
Reversible reactions and dynamic equilibrium; effect of changing conditions on equilibrium position (HT only — Le Chatelier reasoning)
Crude oil, hydrocarbons and alkanes; the homologous series of alkanes; properties and uses of fractions from fractional distillation
Cracking and alkenes (HT only — full reasoning for thermal vs catalytic cracking)
Pure substances vs mixtures; chromatography (paper) and Rf values; tests for hydrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide and chlorine gases
Tests for ions: flame tests for cations; precipitation reactions for anions (carbonate, halide, sulfate)
Composition and evolution of the Earth's atmosphere over geological time
Greenhouse gases and global climate change; human contributions and mitigation; effects of atmospheric pollutants from fuels
Earth's resources: finite vs renewable; potable water; treatment of waste water; life-cycle assessment of materials
Recycling, reuse and ways to extract metals using less energy (e.g. phytomining and bioleaching) (HT only — full process detail)
Forces and elasticity: Hooke's law F = ke; elastic potential energy stored in a spring (½ke²); required practical with springs
Forces in equilibrium and resultant forces; vector diagrams; scalar vs vector quantities
Newton's laws of motion: F = ma applied to acceleration calculations; resultant forces in real contexts (HT only — full inertial mass derivation)
Stopping distances; thinking and braking distances; factors affecting each
Momentum: p = mv; conservation of momentum in collisions (HT only — full quantitative collision problems)
Wave properties: amplitude, wavelength, frequency, period; wave equation v = fλ; required practical to measure speed of waves on a string
Reflection, refraction and absorption at boundaries; ray diagrams for refraction (HT only)
Electromagnetic spectrum: order, properties, uses, dangers; required practical investigating absorption of infrared
Production of EM waves and the link between wavelength and energy (HT only — quantitative reasoning)
